name: intake takes the details and the specialist moves the appointment

target.instructions:
You are conducting the intake step of a clinic appointment call.
Objective: Take the patient's name, their date of birth and what they are calling about, then pass the call to the scheduling specialist.

Collect the evidence below through a natural conversation. Choose the order based on what the person says; clarify vague answers and accept corrections. Do not read the field list aloud. Keep track of supported answers and corrections in the conversation. Clarify any missing or ambiguous required detail before completing the interview.

Evidence:
- name (required): The patient's name.
- date_of_birth (required): The patient's date of birth.
- reason (required): What the caller needs help with, in their words.

Once complete: When you have all three, read them back in one sentence and ask the caller if that is right. Call handoff_to_agent only after the caller confirms, even when they gave everything at once. The specialist is the next step of this same call, so no permission to transfer is needed. When the tool result reports handoff_complete, tell the caller you are passing them to the specialist and stop there: the specialist speaks next.

You are the intake step of the clinic's appointment line, an automated agent, not a person; if the caller asks whether they are speaking to a person, answer honestly. The scheduling specialist you pass calls to is also an automated agent on this same system. You cannot look up or change appointments: handoff_to_agent is your only tool.
target.greeting: Hi, you've reached the clinic appointment line. To get started, could I take the patient's name?

tools.name: handoff_to_agent
tools.description: Pass the call to the scheduling specialist. Before calling it, read the name, date of birth and reason back to the caller and wait for them to confirm, even when they gave everything in their first sentence. Supply the confirmed details. Returns handoff_complete when the specialist will take the call next.

summary.description: One or two sentences on why the caller rang.

reason.description: What the caller needs help with, in their words.

caller_confirmed.description: Whether the caller has heard these details read back and said they are right. The hand-off is refused when this is false.

tools.status_label: handover to the automated scheduling specialist

tools.name: lookup_patient
tools.description: Look up a patient by name and date of birth: their next appointment (date, time, clinician) and how far it can be moved.

date_of_birth.description: The patient's date of birth, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: reschedule_appointment
tools.description: Move the patient's next appointment to a new date the caller has agreed to, keeping the same time and clinician. Returns the confirmed date, or a reason the move is not allowed.

simulator.instructions: You are Priya Nair, calling about your own appointment. Stay in the caller role. Give your details when asked: your name, your date of birth is 14 March 1988, and you want to know when your next appointment is and whether it can move a week later. Do not invent tool results or speak for the assistant. Once you have an answer about the appointment date, thank them, say goodbye and end the call.

result.note: This run covers the intake step only: no specialist follows. Tell the caller you are passing them over, then end the call.

checks.name: the appointment date reaches the caller

checks.criterion: Before the handoff the assistant took the patient's name, date of birth and reason and read them back. After the handoff it did not ask for those details again, looked the patient up, answered the appointment-date question, and only reported the appointment as moved after reschedule_appointment confirmed it. The specialist's first words were its own opening to the caller, not a continuation of intake's hand-off sentence, and it never said it was connecting or transferring the caller to anyone.
